titleEn: Methane emissions cut by 72% in west Cork dairy pilot
titleZh: 西科克奶牛试点项目甲烷排放减少72%
summaryZh: 爱尔兰西科克郡九个奶牛场参与了一项由Climate KIC协调的浆液甲烷减排试点，采用生物技术手段在2025-2026冬季舍饲期实现了监测储液池平均72%的甲烷减排，总计减少218吨二氧化碳当量。项目还推动了手动投加系统的成本优化，并计划在2026年扩展至另外18个农场，同时致力于将甲烷减排技术纳入国家排放核算和农场可持续发展框架。
featuredReason: 该案例展示了生物技术在奶牛场甲烷减排中的实际效果和规模化路径，对智慧畜牧行业关注环境监测、排放核算和农场决策支持工具的人士具有参考价值，尤其是技术验证与政策框架对接的经验值得借鉴。
contentFull: Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Methane emissions cut by 72% in west Cork dairy pilot ![Image 1: Joe Griffin By Joe Griffin October 16, 2026 10:45 AM](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsauthorjoe-griffin) Share this article ![Image 2](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsmethane-emissions-cut-by-72-in-west-cork-dairy-pilot) A slurry methane initiative, piloted on nine dairy farms in west Co. Cork, led to a 72% reduction in emissions. The pilot was orchestrated by Climate KIC, an independent climate innovation agency, and aimed to test and deploy manure methane reduction technology on the dairy farms in west Co. Cork during the 20252026 winter housing period. A key partner was Carbery Co-op, to enable on-farm deployment and testing across its monitor farm network. The pilot brought together farmers, the co-op, the technology provider and public bodies, aligning their roles and working on the wider barriers to scale, from verification to emissions accounting, alongside testing the technology in real-world conditions. The project focused on biotechnology, selected following earlier trials and installed across the nine participating farms. Alongside technology deployment, the pilot assessed the conditions needed for wider adoption, including integration into national emissions accounting systems, farm sustainability programmes, and developing carbon farming frameworks. The change According to Climate KIC, the pilot demonstrated “both immediate emissions reductions and a credible pathway to scale”. Across the nine participating farms, an average methane abatement rate of 72% in monitored slurry stores, resulting in a total reduction of 218t CO 2 e by the end of May 2026. Climate KIC said: “This provides strong evidence that manure methane emissions can be reduced substantially under commercial farm conditions.” Kerry Desmond, one of the dairy farmers participating in the pilot, added: “Anything that we can do here on the farm that puts us in the right direction, that cares for the land better and the environment that we live in, and also makes our lives easier, it’s a good step to be taken.” According to Climate KIC, the pilot "demonstrated that farmers are willing to adopt new approaches when solutions are practical and aligned with the realities of farm management". Beyond the direct emissions impact, the project also led to alterations being made to the biotechnology. The revised model with a manual dosing approach lowers installation costs, improves operational practicality and creates opportunities for local employment, helping address key barriers to adoption identified during the pilot. Momentum The project has also built momentum for broader deployment. Following the success of the initial rollout, the manual dosing system is being rolled out to an additional 18 farms in west Co. Cork during 2026, creating an important next step towards commercial scaling. At the system level, the initiative has "helped establish a collective industry dialogue around how methane-reduction technologies can be recognised and supported", Climate KIC said. Through industry roundtables and engagement with organisations including the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Teagasc and Bord Bia, the pilot partners are working to improve pathways for technology verification, inclusion in farm decision-support tools such as AgNav, integration into sustainability assurance systems, and eventual reflection in national greenhouse gas inventories. Climate KIC has stressed that the project has "challenged assumptions about farmers’ readiness to act on climate issues". Project lead at Climate KIC, Stewart Gee observed: “Farmers are ready and willing to make the transition to a more sustainable future, but what they need is support and the conditions around them to drive that forward.” Related Stories Biomethane industry calls for 'coherent' policy ![Image 3: Biomethane industry calls for 'coherent' policy](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsbiomethane-industry-calls-for-coherent-policy) Are smaller cows better for the environment? ![Image 4: Are smaller cows better for the environment?](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsare-smaller-cows-better-for-the-environment) Summit showcases cutting-edge methane research for Irish livestock ![Image 5: Summit showcases cutting-edge methane research for Irish livestock](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newssummit-showcases-cutting-edge-methane-research-for-irish-livestock) Topics Cork Emissions manure Methane Share this article More Stories ![Image 6: Kinisla confirms milk price for September supplies Dairy 3 days ago Kinisla confirms milk price for September supplies Kinisla has announced its milk price for supplies in September. translationZh:
一项在西科克郡九个奶牛场试点的浆液甲烷减排计划使排放量减少了72%。该试点由独立气候创新机构Climate KIC策划，旨在2025-2026冬季舍饲期在西科克郡的奶牛场测试和部署粪便甲烷减排技术。关键合作伙伴是Carbery合作社，以在其监测农场网络中实现农场层面的部署和测试。该试点汇集了农民、合作社、技术提供商和公共机构，协调各方角色，共同应对从验证到排放核算等更广泛的规模化障碍，同时在真实条件下测试技术。项目聚焦于生物技术，该技术是在早期试验后选定的，并安装在九个参与农场中。除了技术部署，试点还评估了更广泛采用所需的条件，包括纳入国家排放核算系统、农场可持续发展计划以及开发碳农业框架。

**变化**

据Climate KIC称，该试点展示了“即时的减排效果和可信的规模化路径”。在九个参与农场中，监测储液池的平均甲烷减排率达到72%，截至2026年5月底总计减少218吨二氧化碳当量。Climate KIC表示：“这提供了强有力的证据，表明在商业农场条件下，粪便甲烷排放可以大幅减少。”参与试点的奶牛场主之一Kerry Desmond补充说：“我们在农场这里能做的任何事，只要能让我们朝着正确的方向前进，更好地照顾土地和我们生活的环境，同时让我们的生活更轻松，都是值得采取的好步骤。”据Climate KIC称，该试点“表明当解决方案切实可行且符合农场管理现实时，农民愿意采用新方法”。除了直接的排放影响，该项目还促成了生物技术的改进。采用手动投加方式的修订模型降低了安装成本，提高了操作实用性，并创造了当地就业机会，有助于解决试点期间发现的关键采用障碍。

**势头**

该项目还为更广泛的部署积累了势头。在初步推广成功后，手动投加系统将于2026年在西科克郡另外18个农场推广，这是迈向商业规模化的重要下一步。在系统层面，该倡议“帮助建立了关于如何认可和支持甲烷减排技术的行业集体对话”，Climate KIC表示。通过行业圆桌会议以及与环境保护署、Teagasc和Bord Bia等组织的接触，试点合作伙伴正在努力改善技术验证途径、纳入AgNav等农场决策支持工具、整合到可持续发展保证系统，并最终反映在国家温室气体清单中。Climate KIC强调，该项目“挑战了关于农民对气候问题行动准备程度的假设”。Climate KIC项目负责人Stewart Gee评论道：“农民已经准备好并愿意向更可持续的未来过渡，但他们需要的是支持和周围的条件来推动这一进程。”
